q: In circular motion, there are two different ____ that are encountered.
e: The analysis of circular motion involves understanding both centripetal and centrifugal forces.

q: They are centripetal force and ____ force.
e: Centrifugal force is the apparent outward force experienced in a rotating reference frame.

q: Centripetal force is the force acting towards the centre of the circular path, whereas the centrifugal force appears to act in a direction pointing ____ from the centre.
e: Centrifugal force is perceived as pushing objects radially outward.

q: Consider, for example, a person whirls a ball on the end of a string in a horizontal circle around his ____.
e: This is a common physical demonstration of uniform circular motion.

q: The person pulls the string to exert an ____ force on the ball.
e: The person must pull inward to provide the necessary centripetal force.

q: According to Newton's third law, the ball exerts a ____ force on the hand.
e: Every action force has an equal and opposite reaction force acting on the other object.

q: There is a misconception that this reaction force is the outward-directed ____ force acting on the ball.
e: The reaction force acts on the hand, not on the ball itself as an outward centrifugal force.

q: Except centripetal force, there is no other force acting on the ball along the ____.
e: In an ideal horizontal circle, tension is the only force acting along the radial axis.

q: When a car is moving with constant velocity along a straight road, there is no ____ force on the person.
e: According to Newton's first law, constant velocity implies a net force of zero.

q: Hence, the person feels ____ force acting on him when moving at constant velocity in a straight line.
e: Without acceleration, there are no unbalanced forces for the person to feel.

q: However, when the car moves around a curve the person feels an ____ force exerted on him.
e: The passenger's inertia resists the change in direction, feeling like an outward push.

q: This outward feeling is the centrifugal force caused by the effect of ____.
e: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist changes to its state of motion.

q: Actually, the centrifugal force is not a ____ force.
e: It does not arise from any physical interaction between objects.

q: It is an apparent or ____ force which is equal and opposite to the centripetal force.
e: Fictitious forces only appear when observing from an accelerating (rotating) frame of reference.

q: Although centrifugal force is not a real force, the concept can be applied in rotating devices, such as centrifuges, washing machines, centrifugal pumps, centrifugal governors and centrifugal ____.
e: Centrifugal clutches engage automatically as the engine speed increases.

q: A centrifuge is a piece of equipment that puts an object in rotation around a fixed ____.
e: The central axis is the point around which the centrifuge spins.

q: In a laboratory centrifuge, the radial acceleration causes denser particles to settle to the ____ of the tube.
e: Higher density materials experience a greater net force pushing them outward to the bottom.

q: In a laboratory centrifuge, low density substances rise to the ____ of the tube.
e: Less dense materials are displaced inward toward the top or center of rotation.

q: The effect of denser particles settling and low density substances rising in a centrifuge is known as the ____ principle.
e: Sedimentation is the process of settling or being deposited as sediment.

q: A centrifugal pump is a hydraulic machine which converts mechanical energy into ____ energy by the use of centrifugal force.
e: The pump increases the pressure (hydraulic energy) of the fluid.

q: The rotating ____ in a centrifugal pump moves water or other fluids by using centrifugal force.
e: The impeller is the rotating component that transfers energy to the fluid.

q: The centrifugal action of a washing machine is used in ____ drying the clothes.
e: The spin cycle rotates the drum rapidly to extract water.

q: In a washing machine, excess water is removed completely with the help of ____ force.
e: The water is forced out through the holes in the drum due to its inertia.

q: The centrifugal governor is a device used to measure and regulate the ____ of a machine, such as an engine.
e: Governors automatically adjust fuel or steam flow to maintain a constant engine speed.

q: The centrifugal governors consist of two balls of equal mass, which are attached to the ____.
e: The flyballs are mounted on hinged arms that pivot as speed changes.

q: As the engine is working, these balls also revolve around the ____ at a certain speed.
e: The spindle is the central rotating shaft driven by the engine.

q: Centripetal force is directed towards the axis of rotation or centre of ____.
e: The center of curvature is the geometric center of the circular path.

q: Centrifugal force acts radially ____ from the centre of the circle.
e: It is perceived as pushing outward, opposite to the centripetal force.

q: Centrifugal force results from the effect of ____.
e: It is a consequence of an object's mass resisting a change in its directional velocity.

q: If a car is travelling through a curve, the centripetal force provided by the force of ____ between the tires and road allows the car to negotiate the turn.
e: Static friction prevents the tires from sliding laterally across the road surface.

q: When a car in motion takes a sudden turn, passengers experience an ____ push.
e: The passengers' bodies attempt to continue straight while the car turns inward beneath them.

q: This outward push on passengers is due to the ____ force acting on them.
e: From the reference frame of the turning car, this fictitious force appears to push them outward.

q: A satellite orbiting a planet is supported by the ____ force.
e: Gravity acts as the real centripetal force keeping the satellite in orbit.

q: Removing excess water by spin drying clothes is accomplished with the help of ____ force.
e: The apparent outward force separates the water from the fabric.
